question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ |
| $X=6$ | $0.3$ | $0.15$ |

Compute $P(Y=3\,|\,X=2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required probability is given by

$$
P(Y=3\,|\,X=2)=\frac{P(X=2,Y=3)}{P(X=2)}=\frac{f(2,3)}{{f}_{X}(2)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{X}(x)$ is the marginal distribution of $X.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(2) & =0.05+0.25 \\  & =0.30\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,3)=0.25.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{X}(2)=0.30$ and $f(2,3)=0.25$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=3\,|\,X=2) & =\frac{f(2,3)}{{f}_{X}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.25}{0.30} \\  & ≈0.83.\end{aligned}
$$
